recap_title: 🎯 Quick & Visual Recap: MIT App Inventor (Senior)
recap_subtitle: Welcome, hero! This is a quick review supported by programming examples and illustrations for each session you learned in the course to help you remember the concepts with ease and fun and prepare for the super exam! 🚀🌟

points.title: Familiarity with the MIT App Inventor environment
points.desc: A free environment for designing and programming smartphone applications using a drag-and-drop block system. It consists of the Designer screen and the Blocks screen.

points.title: Add basic elements (Button & Label)
points.desc: Use Label to display text and instructions on the screen, and use Button to receive user clicks and activate code commands.
points.code:
whenButton1.Click
do set Label1.Text to “Welcome to the world of application programming!”
points.example: Change the screen background color when you press the welcome button.

points.title: Organize your screen with Layouts
points.desc: Use HorizontalArrangement to arrange items horizontally, and TableArrangement to arrange them in the form of a table to organize the application screen like a professional.

points.title: Use Canvas for drawing and painting
points.desc: The Canvas element allows the user to draw freely with his finger, and change the colors of the drawing when touching the buttons of the specified colors.
points.code:
when Canvas1.Dragged (startX, startY, prevX, prevY, currentX, currentY)
do call Canvas1.DrawLine (prevX, prevY, currentX, currentY)
points.example: A smart drawing board application (Whiteboard Paint App) that draws colored lines with a finger movement.

sessions.session_title: Session 3: ImageSprites & Touching (Catch the Cat Game)

points.title: Add animated objects (ImageSprite)
points.desc: An animated object placed inside Canvas that has movement, speed, direction, and touch interaction properties.

points.title: Programming to touch the object (Touch Event)
points.desc: Touch programming to increase points and change the object's location randomly by simply touching it to simulate the challenge of interactive games.
points.code:
when ImageSprite1.Touched (x, y)
do set global score to (get global score + 1)
call ImageSprite1.MoveTo (random integer 1 to 300, random integer 1 to 300)
points.example: Fast-paced Catch the Cat Game to increase points with every successful touch.

points.title: SpeechRecognizer
points.desc: An invisible tool that uses Google's engine to convert the user's voice speech into written text that can be processed programmatically.

points.title: Convert text to speech (TextToSpeech)
points.desc: A tool that pronounces written texts with clear and excellent human voices to speak to the user automatically.
points.code:
when SpeechRecognizer1.AfterGettingText (result)
do set Label_Result.Text to get result
call TextToSpeech1.Speak (join "I said: " get result)
points.example: The Speech Calculator application performs mathematical operations and pronounces the result vocally to the user.

points.title: Add and manage multiple screens
points.desc: How to move between screens using opening and closing screen blocks to coordinate the steps of using the application.

points.title: Data validation and confidentiality
points.desc: Use PasswordTextBox to protect passwords, and check email and password match before allowing access.
points.example: Implement a secure login screen to verify the student's ID and password before opening the home screen.

sessions.session_title: Session 6: Advanced Screens & Local DB (TinyDB Profile App)

points.title: Local database (TinyDB)
points.desc: An invisible element to store and save user data such as texts and images permanently in the phone's memory even when the application is closed.

points.title: Recover saved data
points.desc: Read previously stored data and automatically fill it in the application interface to enhance the personalized user experience.
points.example: The Profile Editor application permanently saves the student's name, age, and personal photo.

sessions.session_title: Session 7: Edge Collisions & Bounce Physics (Pong Ball Game)

points.title: Program Ball and Collision (Ball Component)
points.desc: A movable spherical element placed inside the Canvas that has the properties of an automatic and physical bounce when it hits the edges and borders of screens.

points.title: Calculating the bounce angle upon collision
points.desc: Programming the ball's bounce upon contact with a moving player's racket to create realistic and entertaining interactive gaming experiences.
points.code:
when Ball1.CollidedWith (other)
do set Ball1.Heading to (360 - get Ball1.Heading)
call Sound_Ping.Play
points.example: Classic Ping Pong Game to calculate points and save the best score with a record.

sessions.session_title: Session 8: Data Lists & ListView (To-Do List App)

points.title: Managing arrays and lists
points.desc: Using arrays to store and group multiple texts or tasks into a single structured data variable.

points.title: Display data in ListView
points.desc: An interactive element that displays a matrix of tasks on the screen in an organized manner that allows the user to review and delete items with one click.
points.code:
when Button_Add.Click
do add items to list (list = get global taskList, item = TextBox_NewTask.Text)
set ListView_Tasks.Elements to get global taskList
set TextBox_NewTask.Text to ""
points.example: To-Do List App allows you to write new tasks, review them, and delete completed tasks.

sessions.session_title: Session 9: Random Choice Logic (Rock Paper Scissors Game)

points.title: Random selection from lists
points.desc: A tool for selecting a completely random item from a programming list, and it is widely used in programming artificial intelligence for competitive games.

points.title: Programming comparison rules and calculating the winner
points.desc: Use code terms to compare the user's choice with a random phone choice and determine the winner while adding an exciting sound.
points.example: Interactive rock-paper-scissors game against smartphone with win-loss statistics calculation.

sessions.session_title: Session 10: Multi-screen Advanced Architecture (Medical Clinic App)

points.title: Large application architecture and UX standards
points.desc: Designing an integrated system consisting of 6 connected screens and passing data between the screens to register patients and book appointments.
blocksArray: open another screen with start value

points.title: Digital clinic and pharmacy reservation system
points.desc: Building specialized screens for clinics to display available specialties and bill calculations for the patient, and a screen for the pharmacy to purchase medications.
points.example: The integrated smart doctor’s clinic application (Smart Clinic App) for booking clinics and dispensing medical prescriptions.

sessions.session_title: Session 11: Generative AI & Web Services (ChatGPT Assistant)

points.title: Introduction to integrating artificial intelligence with applications
points.desc: Use web tools to connect the app with intelligent AI models to send questions and receive genius text answers.

points.title: Programming your AI Assistant
points.desc: Combine Generative AI with SpeechRecognizer to create an intelligent assistant that listens, questions, and answers with its voice.
points.code:
when ChatBot1.GotResponse (response)
do set Label_AIResponse.Text to get response
call TextToSpeech1.Speak (get response)
points.example: ChatGPT Personal Assistant app for voice queries and homework assignments.

sessions.session_title: Session 12: Advanced AI Components (ImageCreator DALL-E App)

points.title: Image generation with artificial intelligence (ImageBot)
points.desc: A very advanced component that allows the application to send a text description in English to image generation servers to design and display an instant painting.

points.title: Download and view generated artboards
points.desc: Receive the link of the AI-generated image and set it as Canvas wallpaper or save it to the phone memory automatically.
points.code:
when Button_Generate.Click
do call ImageBot1.CreateImage (prompt = TextBox_Prompt.Text)

when ImageBot1.ImageCreated (image)
do set Image_Result.Picture to get image
points.example: AI Image Creator Studio generates amazing paintings from just written word descriptions.
